title: Bacterial mucosal immunotherapy for prevention of lower respiratory tract infections in preterm born infants: follow up studies
official: Bacterial mucosal immunotherapy for prevention of lower respiratory tract infections in preterm born infants: follow up studies
summary:
Background and study aims
A significant proportion of infants born at ≤29+6 weeks’ gestation develop lung disease during the neonatal period and are at risk of lung disease later in childhood and adulthood. Respiratory viral infections after discharge from the neonatal unit can worsen existing lung disease and lead to increased healthcare use, including hospital admissions. The BALLOON trial (https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN14019493) is investigating whether treatment with Backtek (MV130) can reduce the risk of unscheduled visits to healthcare professionals for lower respiratory tract infections compared with placebo.

This follow-up study aims to assess whether Backtek has a continuing effect for at least six months after treatment has stopped and whether there are any neurodevelopmental safety issues at two years' corrected age. The study will compare Backtek with placebo to determine its effects on longer-term respiratory outcomes, neurodevelopmental outcomes and growth in preterm-born children.

Who can participate?
Infants born at less than 30 weeks’ gestation who were recruited to the main BALLOON clinical trial and whose parents or guardians consented to follow-up. Infants must be expected to survive to 18 months and 2 years' corrected age.

What does the study involve?
Participants will be followed up at 18 months and 2 years' corrected age. Parents or guardians will be asked whether they are willing to be contacted for follow-up assessments.

At 18 months' corrected age, parents or guardians will be asked to complete a respiratory questionnaire collecting information on lower respiratory tract infections, wheezing, hospital admissions, medication use and related respiratory outcomes. Growth information will be collected from the Personal Child Health Record ("Red Book") and routine follow-up assessments conducted by local neonatal units.

At 2 years' corrected age, parents or guardians will be asked to complete respiratory questionnaires and the Parent Report of Children's Abilities-Revised (PARCA-R) neurodevelopmental questionnaire. Growth information will again be collected from the Personal Child Health Record and local neonatal unit follow-up assessments.

For children for whom questionnaire data are unavailable, information on symptoms, development, growth, hospital admissions and medication use will be obtained from hospital or general practitioner records. Information on hospital admissions and outpatient attendances will also be obtained from NHS England records. Neonatal and neurodevelopmental data at 2 years' corrected age will be obtained from the Neonatal Research Database via the National Database Analyses Unit at Imperial College London.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
The protocol states that the study aims to assess longer-term respiratory outcomes, neurodevelopmental outcomes and growth in preterm-born children who participated in the BALLOON trial. Possible benefits and risks of participating are not specified.

Where is the study run from?
Cardiff University, UK

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
November 2026 to June 2030.

Who is funding the study?
1. The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Efficacy and Mechanism Evaluation (EME) Programme
2. Inmunotek Pharma Ltd.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Sarah Kotecha, Cardiff University, kotechasj@cardiff.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Infants born at <30 weeks’ gestation who are recruited to the main BALLOON Clinical Trial (https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN14019493) who have consented to follow up
2. Anticipated survival to 18 months and 2 years corrected age
Exclusion criteria:
Not meeting the key inclusion criteria
